steps.label: 2.3 The Dot Product
steps.subtitle: Definition (Scalar Product)
steps.bodyHtml:
For vectors $\mathbf{u}=\langle u_1,u_2,u_3\rangle$ and $\mathbf{v}=\langle v_1,v_2,v_3\rangle$:
            $$\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}=u_1v_1+u_2v_2+u_3v_3.$$
            The result is a scalar

steps.label: 2.3 The Dot Product
steps.subtitle: Geometric Form (Angle)
steps.bodyHtml:
If $\theta$ is the angle between nonzero vectors $\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}$,
            $$\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}=||\mathbf{u}||\,||\mathbf{v}||\cos\theta.$$
            Useful for finding angles.

steps.label: 2.3 The Dot Product
steps.subtitle: Orthogonal Vectors
steps.bodyHtml:
Vectors are orthogonal iff
            $$\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}=0.$$
            Useful perpendicularity test.

steps.label: 2.3 The Dot Product
steps.subtitle: Projection
steps.bodyHtml:
The projection of $\mathbf{v}$ onto $\mathbf{u}$ is
            $$\text{proj}_{\mathbf{u}}\,\mathbf{v}=\frac{\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{u}}{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{u}}\mathbf{u}.$$
            component of one vector along another

steps.label: 2.4 The Cross Product
steps.subtitle: Definition (Vector Product)
steps.bodyHtml:
For $\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}\in\mathbb{R}^3$,
            $\mathbf{u}\times\mathbf{v}$ is a vector orthogonal to both $\mathbf{u}$ & $\mathbf{v}$.
            Its direction follows the right-hand rule.

steps.label: 2.4 The Cross Product
steps.subtitle: Determinant Formula
steps.bodyHtml:
$$\mathbf{u}\times\mathbf{v}=\begin{vmatrix}
            \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k}\\
            u_1 & u_2 & u_3\\
            v_1 & v_2 & v_3
            \end{vmatrix}.$$
            computational form

steps.label: 2.4 The Cross Product
steps.subtitle: Magnitude (Area)
steps.bodyHtml:
$$||\mathbf{u}\times\mathbf{v}||=||\mathbf{u}||\,||\mathbf{v}||\sin\theta,$$
            the area of parallelogram with sides $\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}$.

steps.label: 2.4 The Cross Product
steps.subtitle: Special Properties
steps.bodyHtml:
If $\mathbf{u}\times\mathbf{v}=0$, then $\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}$ are parallel, zero area.
            Triple scalar product:
            $$\mathbf{u}\cdot(\mathbf{v}\times\mathbf{w})$$
            gives volume of parallelepiped.
